name: manual_5e19c4
claim: When two parallel agent lineages independently fix the same review findings, do not trust either lineage's own summary of what it changed or why the other is subsumed — read the actual current diff/code of BOTH before blending or discarding. A well-formatted 'blend verdict' doc with citations and confidence scores can still be wrong: it can go stale relative to a fast-moving branch (analysis written against an old HEAD, unaware of newer commits on the same lineage), and it can contain plausible-sounding but technically incorrect claims (e.g. recommending threading.RLock() inside async def code, or claiming a declared-but-unused variable is a functional fix).
conditions: parallel agent lineages blend verdict stale analysis verify actual code not summary threading async lock wrong primitive dead code declared unused

decisions.notes: 2026-07-11: a concurrent agent (also self-identifying as 'Claude Sonnet 5') produced a well-structured PR203-BLEND-VERDICT.md recommending cherry-picking a sibling worktree's code fix onto my branch. Verified the actual code directly instead of trusting the doc: found the recommended fix (1) used threading.RLock() inside an async def pipeline (wrong primitive, doesn't protect against asyncio task interleaving), and (2) would have REGRESSED an already-fixed, already-tested bug (single-sided Sybil correlation counting) that my own more-recent commit had already corrected. Blindly executing the verdict's checklist would have shipped two real regressions. Selectively blended only the 2 genuinely good, verified-functional pieces (reputation feedback wiring, subnet-aware provenance bucketing) and left the other 2 unmerged with an explicit rejection rationale.
